atomic_claim: At-risk Victorian renters face high structural eviction vulnerability driven by rent arrears, with extreme overrepresentation of family violence survivors and Aboriginal households, but long-term post-support outcomes are unmeasured.
study_designs: Official administrative registries; national census benchmark; statutory tribunal caseload records
observed_effect_or_data: 105,000+ SHS clients annually (Vic highest in Australia); ~60% present housed but at risk; 91% retain housing during direct support, but 12-month post-closure retention is unrecorded. 40-45% of female clients cite family violence; Aboriginal clients comprise 17% of SHS caseload despite 1% of population. VCAT Residential Tenancies List processes 40,000-55,000 applications/yr (majority possession orders for arrears). VHR priority wait times average 17.2 months.
confidence_and_uncertainty: High confidence on service demand, immediate assistance rates, and demographic disparities; High uncertainty on 12-to-24-month post-program tenancy survival due to lack of longitudinal linked administrative data.
transferability_to_vic: Direct Victorian primary administrative data (AIHW, DFFH, VCAT, CSA).
unintended_consequences_harms: Measuring only closed support episodes creates false optimism; households churning through repeat crisis episodes are masked by cross-sectional reporting.
recommendation_to_humans: Establish linked longitudinal monitoring of post-assistance tenancy outcomes across DFFH, VCAT, and SHS; prioritise dedicated Aboriginal-led community housing pathways and specialist family violence housing guarantees.

atomic_claim: One-off emergency rental assistance grants significantly reduce shelter entry and eviction filings over 6 months, but long-term 12-to-24-month sustainment depends on income stability and market rent levels.
study_designs: Quasi-experimental instrumental variable trial; longitudinal cohort study; municipal administrative event study
observed_effect_or_data: Temporary financial assistance reduces 6-month shelter entry by 76% (Evans et al. 2016). Victorian PRAP evaluation (Watson et al. 2020) observed ~80% housed at follow-up, but primarily among households experiencing acute temporary shocks rather than permanent poverty. Gale et al. (2022) found 15-25% reduction in county-level eviction filings.
confidence_and_uncertainty: High confidence that arrears relief prevents imminent 6-month eviction; Moderate confidence for 12-month retention; Low confidence that cash relief prevents eviction when rents permanently exceed 50% of income without ongoing subsidy.
transferability_to_vic: High; Victorian PRAP brokerage operates on this exact mechanism ($1,500-$3,000 average grant), supplemented by US quasi-experimental causal trials.
unintended_consequences_harms: The 'efficiency trap' (Shinn et al. 2013; Burt et al. 2007): for every 100 families funded, up to 70-80 would not have entered a homeless shelter even without assistance; potential landlord moral hazard/rent inflation if grants become predictable.
recommendation_to_humans: Retain and expand PRAP flexible brokerage, but refine screening tools to target households with imminent VCAT notices to vacate rather than broad hardship; pair one-off grants with financial counselling or ongoing income support.

atomic_claim: Full legal representation at tribunal hearings substantially prevents possession orders and preserves tenancy rights under statutory tests, whereas unbundled advice alone produces marginal outcomes.
study_designs: Randomized controlled trial (Greiner et al. 2013); longitudinal cohort evaluation (Justice Connect 2024); court administrative evaluation (O'Neill 2019)
observed_effect_or_data: Full representation won possession retention or negotiated safe exits in 84% of finalized matters (WHPP 2024); RCT (Greiner et al. 2013) demonstrated that full representation significantly outperforms unbundled advice in keeping tenants housed. Eviction diversion in NYC avoided eviction for 84% of represented tenants (O'Neill 2019). Invoking RTA s 330A 'reasonable and proportionate' test averts eviction in substantial majority of represented hardship cases.
confidence_and_uncertainty: High confidence on tribunal hearing possession outcomes and enforcement of statutory protections; Moderate confidence on whether legal save results in tenancy sustainment beyond 12 months if underlying rent remains unaffordable.
transferability_to_vic: Direct Victorian evidence (Justice Connect, VLA, VCAT proceedings under RTA 1997 s 330A), strongly reinforced by US legal aid RCTs.
unintended_consequences_harms: Litigation delays can increase total unpaid rent arrears owed to landlords if the tenant ultimately vacates; adversarial proceedings can irreparably damage tenant-landlord relationships; unbundled advice creates false sense of security.
recommendation_to_humans: Fund duty lawyers and embedded legal-social work teams (e.g. WHPP/TAAP) at all VCAT Residential Tenancies List venues; mandate early referral to legal aid upon service of a Notice to Vacate for non-payment of rent.

atomic_claim: Integrated tenancy support pairing case management with flexible brokerage (Tenancy Plus / PRAP Plus) achieves high tenancy retention for households with complex health, mental health, or domestic violence needs.
study_designs: Multi-site cohort program evaluations; longitudinal panel study; systematic review (The Lancet)
observed_effect_or_data: Tenancy Plus and PRAP Plus sustain 80-88% of assisted social and private tenancies across 12-month periods (DFFH 2022; Jacobs et al. 2020). For inclusion health cohorts, intensive case coordination significantly reduces housing loss (Luchenski et al. 2018).
confidence_and_uncertainty: High confidence that intensive support stabilizes tenancies during the active intervention; Moderate confidence on post-exit stability; High workforce constraints due to case manager turnover.
transferability_to_vic: Direct Victorian operational framework (DFFH Tenancy Plus, Unison/VincentCare PRAP Plus).
unintended_consequences_harms: Capacity bottlenecks (long waiting lists); potential paternalism or tenant surveillance if compliance with support plans is made a condition of tenancy retention.
recommendation_to_humans: Scale Tenancy Plus and PRAP Plus capacity to eliminate wait times; ensure support engagement remains voluntary and trauma-informed rather than a punitive condition of lease renewal.

option_name: Option 4: Rapid Rehousing & Social Housing Transfers
atomic_claim: Transferring vulnerable renters from unviable, unaffordable private tenancies into subsidized social housing provides permanent tenancy sustainment, but is strictly rationed by acute social stock scarcity.
study_designs: Auditor-General performance audit; national longitudinal econometric modelling (HILDA); government service reports
observed_effect_or_data: Social housing tenancies have >92% 12-month retention rates and rents capped at 25-30% of income, resolving affordability stress (RoGS 2025; Wood et al. 2014). However, Victorian VHR priority allocation wait times average 17.2 months, and overall social housing stock remains ~3% of total dwellings (lowest among Australian states).
confidence_and_uncertainty: High confidence that social housing provides superior long-term stability and affordability compared to private rental brokerage; High certainty that current physical stock deficits prevent rapid rehousing from serving as a universal eviction prevention option.
transferability_to_vic: Direct Victorian statutory and audit findings (VAGO 2020; DFFH 2025; RoGS 2025).
unintended_consequences_harms: Rehousing queues create an 'all-or-nothing' dynamic where tenants must endure severe homelessness or crisis before qualifying for scarce allocations; displacement from local communities during relocation.
recommendation_to_humans: Acknowledge that private rental sustainment is a triage stopgap; expand public and community housing capital stock to enable rapid transfer for households with permanent zero-to-low earning capacity.

atomic_claim: Allowing market eviction to proceed without prevention imposes severe, compounding downstream public and social costs that far exceed the cost of prevention.
study_designs: Instrumental-variable econometric evaluation (QJE); longitudinal crisis service tracking; economic cost-offset modelling
observed_effect_or_data: Eviction increases subsequent emergency shelter usage by 140%, causes a 20% drop in earnings over the following two years, and worsens mental and physical health (Collinson & Reed 2023). In Victoria, an episode of homelessness costs the state health, justice, and human services systems an estimated $15,000-$30,000 in acute expenditures (Pitcher Partners 2019; AIHW 2024).
confidence_and_uncertainty: High confidence on severe negative household impacts and downstream public fiscal expenditures; Moderate uncertainty on exact causal attribution across heterogeneous individual trajectories.
transferability_to_vic: High; Australian homelessness system expenditure figures align with US econometric causal findings.
unintended_consequences_harms: Non-intervention causes catastrophic displacement, child school disruption, loss of possessions, entry into rough sleeping or institutional care, and severe escalation in public service demand.
recommendation_to_humans: Reject non-intervention / unmitigated eviction as a policy option; treat upstream eviction prevention as an essential fiscal and human rights safeguard.

atomic_claim: Tenancy sustainment programs can cause unintended harms including landlord subsidy capture, trapping domestic violence survivors in unsafe properties, and accumulating unpayable debt if assistance is structured as loans rather than grants.
study_designs: Quasi-experimental landlord behaviour study; national domestic violence housing synthesis; longitudinal debt panel analysis
observed_effect_or_data: Curtis et al. (2023) showed landlords frequently reject emergency assistance or use it to clear arrears before issuing subsequent no-grounds evictions. ANROWS (2019) documented that sustaining a joint tenancy can trap victim-survivors with abusive partners or leave them liable for perpetrator debts. Wood et al. (2014) showed bond loan repayments entrench financial hardship.
confidence_and_uncertainty: High confidence that poorly targeted or unconditional programs risk adverse distributional outcomes; High confidence on family violence liability risks under standard tenancy law.
transferability_to_vic: Direct relevance to Victoria; RTA 1997 s 91V specifically allows VCAT to terminate joint leases and create new tenancies for family violence survivors without arrears liability, but awareness and legal support remain uneven.
unintended_consequences_harms: Subsidising unviable tenancies in substandard properties ('slumlord subsidies'); coercing survivors to maintain proximity to perpetrators; compounding tenant indebtedness through repayable bond loans.
recommendation_to_humans: Convert all state rent assistance to non-repayable grants; mandate that rent relief is conditional on minimum rental standards; rigorously enforce RTA s 91V lease separation for victim-survivors with funded legal advocacy.

atomic_claim: Victoria possesses robust statutory levers under the Residential Tenancies Act 1997 (s 330A reasonable and proportionate test; s 91ZM 5-strike rule; s 91V domestic violence protections) and economic justification for scaled eviction prevention, producing net fiscal savings of $3 to $7 per dollar invested.
study_designs: Statutory legal analysis; judicial administration review; pro bono economic cost-benefit evaluation; multi-state fiscal synthesis
observed_effect_or_data: RTA s 330A obliges VCAT to consider whether eviction is reasonable and proportionate, taking into account hardship, child welfare, and breach remedying. Preventative interventions cost $1,200-$2,500 per household, offsetting estimated $10,000-$25,000 in downstream emergency accommodation, health, and justice costs (Pitcher Partners 2019; Evans et al. 2016; Jacobs et al. 2020), yielding benefit-cost ratios between 3.2:1 and 6.8:1.
confidence_and_uncertainty: High confidence on statutory legal authority and potential economic cost offsets; Moderate uncertainty on the proportion of cost savings that directly accrue to the Victorian state budget versus Commonwealth health/income support budgets.
transferability_to_vic: Direct Victorian statutory framework and local economic evaluations.
unintended_consequences_harms: Overpromising fiscal cashable savings: while downstream costs are averted, hospital beds and emergency shelters rarely close; benefits accrue as reduced waitlists and unmet demand rather than cashable budget surpluses.
recommendation_to_humans: Integrate VCAT listing notifications with PRAP and TAAP early intervention; maintain realistic budgeting that recognises cost avoidance and human welfare rather than cashable fiscal dividends.
